entries.originalText: It is good for us that we sometimes have sorrows and adversities, for they often make a man lay to heart that he is only a stranger and sojourner, and may not put his trust in any worldly thing.
entries.modernizedText: It is good for us sometimes to have sorrows and adversities, for they often make a person take to heart that he is only a stranger and sojourner and may not put his trust in any worldly thing.

entries.originalText: It is good that we sometimes endure contradictions, and are hardly and unfairly judged, when we do and mean what is good.
entries.modernizedText: It is good that we sometimes endure contradiction and are harshly and unfairly judged when we do and intend what is good.

entries.originalText: For these things help us to be humble, and shield us from vain-glory.
entries.modernizedText: For these things help us to be humble and shield us from vainglory.

entries.originalText: For then we seek the more earnestly the witness of God, when men speak evil of us falsely, and give us no credit for good.
entries.modernizedText: For then we seek the witness of God more earnestly, when people speak evil of us falsely and give us no credit for good.

entries.originalText: Therefore ought a man to rest wholly upon God, so that he needeth not seek much comfort at the hand of men.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, a person ought to rest wholly on God so that he need not seek much comfort from others.

entries.originalText: When a man who feareth God is afflicted or tried or oppressed with evil thoughts, then he seeth that God is the more necessary unto him, since without God he can do no good thing.
entries.modernizedText: When a person who fears God is afflicted, tried, or oppressed with evil thoughts, he sees that God is all the more necessary to him, since without God he can do no good thing.

entries.originalText: Then he is heavy of heart, he groaneth, he crieth out for the very disquietness of his heart.
entries.modernizedText: Then he is heavy of heart; he groans and cries out because of the very unrest of his heart.

entries.originalText: Then he groweth weary of life, and would fain depart and be with Christ.
entries.modernizedText: Then he grows weary of life and longs to depart and be with Christ.

entries.originalText: By all this he is taught that in the world there can be no perfect security or fulness of peace.
entries.modernizedText: By all this he is taught that in the world there can be no perfect security or fullness of peace.
